summary_sentence: One degree of latitude is approx. 60.04 nautical miles (111.20 km) anywhere on Earth — but one degree of longitude at London's latitude is only approx. 37.4 nautical miles (69.2 km), because the longitude lines converge toward the poles.
quick_answer: The Latitude Degrees to Nautical Miles calculator converts an angle of latitude into the surface distance it represents. body.t: At London's latitude (51.5072° N), one degree of longitude spans approx. 69.2 km — 37.4 nautical miles — against 60.04 nautical miles for a degree of latitude at the same place. The shrinkage factor is simply cos(latitude), and it is why east–west distances can never be converted with the latitude rule of thumb.

London (51.5072° N) and Rome (41.9028° N) differ by approx. 9.6 degrees of latitude — about 577 nautical miles (1,068 km) of pure north–south arc. The full city-to-city distance is longer, approx. 1,433.8 km, because the longitude difference adds its own share; the latitude part is the piece this calculator isolates.

faq: Why does the calculator say 60.04 and not exactly 60 nautical miles?

Because two true things are being combined. By definition, a nautical mile is one arc-minute, so a degree is exactly 60 nautical miles of angle. But this tool converts angle to surface distance on a sphere with the Earth's mean radius (6,371.0088 km), where one degree of arc measures 111.20 km — and 111.20 km is 60.04 nautical miles by the international 1.852 km definition. The 0.04 is the difference between the ideal definition and the mean Earth.
Is a degree of longitude the same distance?

Only at the equator. Longitude lines meet at the poles, so a degree of longitude shrinks with the cosine of latitude: about 60.04 nautical miles at the equator, 37.4 at London's latitude, and effectively zero at the poles. This calculator's headline conversion is for latitude, where the distance is constant.
What is the difference between a nautical mile and a statute mile?

A nautical mile is 1.852 km exactly (about 6,076 feet); a statute mile is about 1.609 km (5,280 feet). One nautical mile is roughly 1.15 statute miles. Nautical miles persist at sea and in the air because they tie directly to the Earth's angles, as this page shows.
What is a knot in these terms?
One knot is one nautical mile per hour. A vessel making 12 knots covers 12 nautical miles — about 0.2 degrees of latitude — every hour, which is why navigators think in these units.
How far is one minute or one second of latitude?

One arc-minute of latitude is one nautical mile by definition (about 1.85 km); one arc-second is about 30.9 metres. That is why coordinates written to hundredths of a second claim roughly metre-level precision — whether the original measurement deserves it is another question.
Can I convert a whole route with this page?

This page converts latitude spans. For a full point-to-point distance, the Distance Between Two Places calculator applies the complete spherical calculation; this page is the quick north–south component and the explanation behind it.
Does the conversion change between the northern and southern hemispheres?
No. A degree of latitude spans the same arc in either hemisphere; only the sign of the coordinate changes. The convergence effect belongs to longitude, not latitude.
